reasons: Errors are handled with messages for search and import failures.
No tests or other evidence of behavior are visible.
The data source is demo data, so the page is not connected to a real record system.

terms.meaning: A web address on the server that the page sends requests to, such as the search or import address.
Numbers used in India to identify a land holding (khata) and a plot within it (khesra).
A village-level area used in land records.
Made-up data that looks realistic but does not describe a real person or parcel.
A server reply meaning the request conflicts with existing data.

sections.name: File setup, MessageTone
sections.title: Imports and message type
sections.what: Brings in the tools, shared components, labels, and data types. It also defines the three kinds of message the page can show: error, success, or status.
sections.why: Needed so the page can show styled, translated messages about searches and imports.

sections.name: identityForCase
sections.title: Matching a record to the case
sections.what: Compares a record's district, circle, mauza, khata, and khesra with the case. It returns exact match when all parcel numbers agree, partial match when the case has no khesra to compare, and mismatch otherwise.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, but the labels show it lets the user judge how well a record fits the case before importing.
sections.watch_out: An exact match needs a khesra number on the case, so a case without one can only reach partial match.

sections.name: OfficialRecordsContent (part 1)
sections.title: Search state and validation
sections.what: Holds the search results, messages, and loading state. When the search is submitted, it checks that the location fields and at least one parcel number are filled in before calling the server.
sections.why: Stops empty searches before they reach the server and gives the user a clear reason.
sections.watch_out: Blank required fields produce a validation message without contacting the server, so server-side checks are not exercised by these blanks.

sections.name: OfficialRecordsContent (part 2)
sections.title: Running search and import
sections.what: Sends the search to the server and shows how many records came back. It also sends the import request for one record and shows success, already linked, conflict, or error messages.
sections.why: Gives the user feedback for each outcome, including network failures.
sections.watch_out: A conflict is recognized only through the 409 status, so the server must send that code for mismatches.

sections.name: OfficialRecordsContent (part 3)
sections.title: Pre-filled search fields
sections.what: Builds the search fields for district, circle, mauza, khata, and khesra. Each field starts with the value already stored on the case.
sections.why: Saves the user from retyping values that the case already has.
sections.watch_out: Pre-filled values come from the case, so a search may repeat the case's own numbers, even if they are wrong.

sections.name: OfficialRecordsContent (part 4)
sections.title: Search form and messages
sections.what: Draws the search form, the status or error message box, and the heading that appears when more than one record matches.
sections.why: Error messages use an alert role so screen readers announce them immediately.

sections.name: OfficialRecordsContent (part 5)
sections.title: Result cards with record details
sections.what: Draws one card for each result, showing the record name, its parcel details, area, holders, record type, survey stage, remarks, and its match label.
sections.why: Lets the user compare the official record with the case before adding it.
sections.watch_out: The area is formatted with a decimal call, so a result missing an area value would fail to display.

sections.name: OfficialRecordsContent (part 6)
sections.title: Source details and import button
sections.what: Shows the record's provider, provenance, and source reference inside a collapsible section. It also shows a safety note and an add button that is disabled while importing or when the match is a mismatch.
sections.why: Keeps the source trail visible while stopping the user from adding a clearly conflicting record.
sections.watch_out: The disabled button only blocks the page. The server must also refuse mismatched imports.

sections.name: OfficialRecordsPage
sections.title: Page wrapper
sections.what: Connects the page to the case so the content receives the case details and case id.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond loading the case before drawing the content.

summary: Lets the user search official land record copies for a parcel and add a matching record to the case. The records are marked as synthetic demo data, not live or authoritative.
purpose: Compare what the case says about its land parcel with an official-style record, and import one match.
why: Likely reason: the labels state the data is not live and not official, so the page warns the user clearly before they rely on it.
how: The user fills in location and parcel numbers and submits a search. The search sends the form to a search endpoint and shows the results. Each result is compared with the case and labeled as exact, partial, or mismatch. An import button sends the chosen record to an import endpoint. A 409 response means the record conflicts with the case.
inputs: Search form values, the case location and parcel numbers, the chosen language, and the case id from the address.
outputs: A list of matching records with a match label, status messages, and a confirmation when a record is added to the case.
risks: The import button is disabled for mismatches only in the page. The server must also refuse these imports. The records are demo data, so they do not reflect real government records.
debug: If search returns nothing, check that all required fields are filled and that the search endpoint responds. If import fails, check the response status and the import endpoint. If the match label looks wrong, check the case location and parcel numbers against the record.
